note: Effects appeared more consistently in self-reports. Pooled evidence did not support changes in hormone levels, and smaller studies or selective reporting complicated interpretation of behavior outcomes.

headline: A follow-up found agreement for some drug-response measurements across two large cancer-cell screens
title: Consistency of drug profiles and predictors in large-scale cancer cell line data
note: This reanalysis of CCLE and GDSC reported stronger agreement than an earlier comparison for some sensitivity measures and genomic predictors. Conclusions depended on how sensitivity was measured and compared.

headline: 177 ecology meta-analyses checked for the materials needed to redo them
title: Computationally reproducing results from meta-analyses in ecology and evolutionary biology using shared code and data
note: Fifteen percent shared both data and code. The investigators attempted reruns on eligible articles and documented barriers even when materials were provided.

headline: Trial registries and original protocols sometimes gave different primary outcomes
title: Association of Trial Registration With Reporting of Primary Outcomes in Protocols and Publications
note: The study matched ethics protocols, registrations and subsequent publications and assessed whether registration was associated with more complete and consistent outcome reporting.

headline: Three cohorts and 4,021 people found small but repeatable brain differences in depression
title: The neuroanatomy of depression: weak but replicable effects in 4021 individuals from three clinical cohorts
note: The study tested structural MRI differences across independent clinical samples. Some case–control differences were repeatable, with small effect sizes.

headline: 20 countries tested whether people use ignorance as an excuse to share less
title: Wilfully ignoring inconvenient information decreases prosociality across diverse cultures
note: Across 7,978 participants, giving people the option to avoid information led to fewer prosocial choices on average, with variation in behavior across countries.

headline: 21 countries put mental accounting effects through the same set of tests
title: The Robustness of Mental Accounting Across 21 Countries
note: The team tested 5,589 participants. The pooled Bayesian analyses supported the tested scenarios, while 133 of 147 individual effects met the unpooled criterion.

headline: Brain prediction benchmarks tested how both training and validation sample size affect replication
title: Power and reproducibility in the external validation of brain-phenotype predictions
note: Resampling analyses of functional and structural connectivity quantified the effects of training and test sample sizes on whether brain–phenotype predictions held up in external data.

headline: 768 pipelines reconstructed brain networks from resting-state fMRI
title: Systematic evaluation of fMRI data-processing pipelines for consistent functional connectomics
note: Pipelines differed considerably in motion sensitivity, test–retest consistency and sensitivity to differences between participants.

headline: An audit asked how often political science journals made replication materials available
title: Data Availability in Political Science Journals
note: The study compared journal policies with actual availability of replication materials and found that access was uneven.

headline: Economics papers from 13 journals went through a data-and-code reproducibility check
title: Is Economics Research Replicable? Sixty Published Papers From Thirteen Journals Say “Often Not”
note: The audit attempted to regenerate selected headline results from author-provided data and code, documenting both missing materials and instances where the files failed to reproduce results.

headline: UK Biobank retested thousands of earlier genome-wide signals
title: Reproducibility in the UK biobank of genome-wide significant signals discovered in earlier genome-wide association studies
note: Across nine phenotypes, 85% of discovery signals met the authors’ replication criterion. Replication was substantially lower for binary outcomes than for quantitative traits.

headline: More than 23,000 children contributed to a check of the bilingual executive-function advantage
title: The Bilingual Advantage in Children’s Executive Functioning Is Not Related to Language Status: A Meta-Analytic Review
note: The pooled estimate was small across 1,194 effect sizes and indistinguishable from zero under the authors’ adjustment for publication bias.

headline: An independent program’s attempts to repeat published spinal cord injury experiments
title: Replication and reproducibility in spinal cord injury research
note: The program documented successful, partial, unsuccessful and inconclusive replication outcomes. Differences in injury models and outcome procedures mattered for some findings.

headline: Brain–behavior prediction improved with larger samples chiefly when measurements were reliable
title: How measurement noise limits the accuracy of brain-behaviour predictions
note: Using UK Biobank data, the study tested how measurement noise limited predictive accuracy as sample size increased from hundreds to thousands.

headline: Independent teams redid the literature searches and analyses for ten systematic reviews
title: Evaluation of the replicability of systematic reviews with meta-analyses of the effects of health interventions
note: The teams repeated searches, screened papers and re-extracted data without initially seeing original results. They compared the resulting study sets, pooled estimates and confidence intervals with the original reviews.

headline: 607 estimates put the magnitude of loss aversion to a cross-study test
title: Meta-analysis of Empirical Estimates of Loss Aversion
note: The researchers combined estimates from 150 articles. Their estimated mean loss-aversion coefficient was 1.955, with variation across individual studies.

headline: A reanalysis checked whether the power-posing literature supported its claims
title: Power Posing: P-Curving the Evidence
note: The authors re-examined the distribution of significant p-values in the power-posing literature and found insufficient evidential value for the broad claim under their analysis.

headline: Independent labs tested whether holding a warm pack makes people more generous
title: Replication of “Experiencing physical warmth promotes interpersonal warmth” by Williams and Bargh (2008)
note: The teams directly repeated the original gift-choice experiment. No individual lab or pooled estimate supported the predicted increase in choosing a reward for a friend.

headline: Three teams repeated the claim that later practice improves earlier recall
title: Failing the Future: Three Unsuccessful Attempts to Replicate Bem’s ‘Retroactive Facilitation of Recall’ Effect
note: Three preregistered direct replication attempts involving 150 participants failed to reproduce the predicted recall advantage.

headline: Eleven countries tested whether changing experienced rewards alters risky choices
title: Comparing experience- and description-based economic preferences across 11 countries
note: The effect of experienced reward context was observed across all 11 countries, while separately measured risk aversion varied by country.
